html:
John Smith was an English soldier and explorer who helped found Jamestown in Virginia, the first lasting English settlement in North America, and led the colony in 1608 and 1609.

Before Virginia he fought as a soldier of fortune in Europe, against the Ottomans in Hungary and Transylvania, where he was captured and sold as a slave before escaping. He sailed with the Virginia Company in 1607. Late that year he was taken prisoner by the Powhatan chiefdom; his later story that the chief's daughter Pocahontas saved his life is famous but much doubted. As president of the colony he made the settlers work ("he that will not work shall not eat") and traded and bullied the Powhatan for corn.

In 1608 he explored Chesapeake Bay and its rivers in an open boat. He met and wrote about many peoples: the Susquehannock, whom he described as tall and well armed, the Nanticoke, the Rappahannock and their neighbours, and the Manahoac, with whom he fought. His map of Virginia, published in 1612, names their towns and was used for decades. Many small groups, such as the Cuttatawomen and Sekakawon, are known mainly from it.

Hurt by a gunpowder accident, he went home in 1609 and never returned to Virginia. In 1614 he mapped the coast of New England and gave it that name. He spent the rest of his life writing books that promoted English colonies.
